allActiveSoftware.scope: Every source-provided name of every active, non-deprecated cask; installation rank does not cap extended acquisition.

bulkNames.selection: Explicit English given-name/surname category membership on proper-name records; no name splitting or synthetic combinations.

scope.categoryScope: Direct categories and two documented category edges, plus required entity types/manufacturer links. Wikipedia category edges are not an unlimited is-a hierarchy.
scope.pagination: Keyset within disjoint complete URI ranges for large scopes; all ranges including punctuation/non-Latin initials must finish. Ranges are transport partitions, never vocabulary caps.
scope.personScope: Exact English DBpedia actor labels and explicitly listed occupation labels. The full Pantheon 2025 dataset supplies the default notable-person and sports population. Generic DBpedia Athlete traversal is not a practical frequency filter and is not used as a completion shortcut.
scope.purpose: Exact typed English DBpedia labels and scoped product/brand categories. No count-based adoption cap; no frequency guarantee. Reject partial HTTP 200 results.

policy.purpose: Scan every published row to EOF; no HPI, rank, language-count or adoption-count cutoff. Exact source name and QID; groups excluded. Broad occupations never imply a narrower sport or Olympic participation.

Visit every person in every sports occupation of the full Pantheon source. Transport batches never finish a campaign early. Independent DBpedia class/category facts distinguish narrow disciplines and Olympic participation; broad SKATER/ATHLETE labels alone do not.

Retain source evidence for curation. Exclude case/accident subjects and victim-context names from distributed assets; retain independently sourced public-career/historical names even with victim flags. A historical birth date alone is insufficient. No claim to detect every incident or disambiguate all homonyms.

VALUES ?relation { dbp:victim dbp:victims } ?item ?relation ?victim; a dbo:Event. ?victim a dbo:Person.
?item a dbo:Event. VALUES ?metric { dbp:fatalities dbp:injuries dbp:deaths dbo:numberOfDeaths dbo:numberOfInjured } ?item ?metric ?count. FILTER(isNumeric(?count) && ?count > 0)
